technical-data.invention-title: VACUUM PROCESSING APPARATUS WITH LOW PARTICLE GENERATING WAFER HOLDER
APPAREIL DE TRAITEMENT SOUS VIDE AVEC SUPPORT DE PLAQUETTE GENERANT PEU DE PARTICULES

abstract.p: A wafer holder (20) is provided for semiconductor wafer processing that is particularly useful where wafers are held and moved in other than upwardly facing orientations during handling and processing. The holder includes an annular wafer mounting ring (12) that is resiliently mounted to and biased against an annular wafer holder housing (11). A set of latches (20) is pivotally mounted to the mounting ring. The latches are formed of non-metallic latch bodies (31) and have non-metallic front and back rollers (35, 36) thereon which have rolling peripheries (37, 39) that roll over the surface of the mounting ring, along a circular path on which are formed spherical detents (42-44). The rolling peripheries of the rollers conform to the curvature of the detents. The front roller also has a gripping periphery (40) at the outer edge thereof that rolls onto the edge of a wafer held in the holder against the edge of the mounting ring. The mounting ring forms a seal with the backplane of the processing apparatus to prevent plasma from forming around the latches. The mounting ring also registers against a stop to space the wafer from the backplane to protect the device side of the wafer when backside wafer processing is being carried out.

Cette invention concerne un support de plaquette (20) pour le traitement des plaquettes de semi-conducteur, qui est particulièrement utile lorsque les plaquettes sont maintenues dans des orientations autres que tournées avec leur face vers le haut, lors de la manipulation et du traitement. Le support de plaquette comprend un anneau de montage circulaire pour plaquette (12) qui est monté de manière élastique sur un logement de support de plaquette circulaire (11) et qui est pressé contre ce logement. Une série de loquets (20) est montée pivotante sur l'anneau de montage. Ces loquets sont constitués de boîtiers non métalliques (31) et comportent des galets non métalliques avant et arrière (35, 36), ayant des pourtours de roulement (37, 39) roulant sur la surface de l'anneau de montage, selon une trajectoire circulaire, sur laquelle sont formés des crans sphériques (42-44). Les pourtours de roulement des galets épousent la courbure des crans. Le galet avant comporte également sur son bord extérieur un pourtour de serrage (40), qui roule sur le bord de la plaquette maintenue dans le support contre le bord de l'anneau de montage. L'anneau de montage forme un joint d'étanchéité avec la face arrière de l'appareil de traitement, pour éviter que du plasma ne se forme autour des loquets. L'anneau de montage se place également en alignement contre une butée, afin d'écarter la plaquette de la face arrière, en vue de protéger le côté composant électronique de la plaquette, lorsque l'on procède à un traitement de la face postérieure de la plaquette.

description.p: VACUUM PROCESSING APPARATUS W ITH LOW PARTICLE GENERATING WAFER HOLDER

This invention lelates to high vacuum processing and particularly the handling and holding of wafers, particularly semiconductor wafers, for such high vacuum processing More particularly, this invention relates to the avoidance of watei damage, particulate contamination and other problems that arise in semiconductor device manufacturing piocesses in the handling and holding of semiconductor wafers in semiconductor wafer processing equipment
Background ol the Invention:

In semiconductor manufacturing piocesses such as, for example, the sputtering of thin films onto substrates such as silicone oi gallium arsenate w afeis, it is usually necessary to transfer wafers among different process chambeis In some systems, wafers are transferred in a horizontal plane where the wafer typically rests on a tiansfer arm lesembhng a paddle The gravitational force on the wafer and the resulting faction between the wafer and the undei lying supporting element, combined with controlled acceleration of the wafer on the support element, makes possible the use of clamp-free wafer transfer. In some systems, however, for process related and other reasons, wafers are moved in non-horizontal orientations or held in non-horizontal orientations during processmg In such systems, the wafer is locked to and carried by a device called a wafer holder that is equipped with clamping structure or other locking elements to hold the wafer in position on the holder

The locking device of a wafer holder is typically referred to as a latch. The latch exerts pressure on the water to lock the wafer in a fixed position on the holder With certain spring biased latches, for example, the latches exert pressure against a wafer. \\ hich is supported by the multitude of independent tabs or by a wafer mounting ring Friction force betw een such elements and the wafer prevents the wafei from slipping during the motion of the wafer holder

Some wafers of which semiconductois ate made are very fragile, either because of their small thicknesses or because of the nature of the substrate material of which they are made, for example, gallium arsenate wafers, which aie particularly fragile In the final stages of device fabrication, a large number of nearly completed semiconductor devices on a \\ afer adds substantial value to the basic wafer, however, making such wafers very expensive Any bieakage of a wafer at such later stages of fabrication represents a substantial economic loss and contributes a substantial cost to semiconductor device manufacturing Poor function or reliability of the latches that retain the wafers to the holders can result in such breakage
as well as increase the equipment down-time and a loss ot equipment throughput Further, rough operation of the latches can cause the pioduction of paiticulates in the vacuum chambei causing contamination of the wafer, w hich can terfeie with the fabncation ot semiconductoi devices and result in the production of defective devices High vacuum systems aie widely used m technical and commercial applications such as semiconductor device manufactui ing piocesses, which require the performance of the particular process in the absence of air and airborne contaminants An example of such a process is the sputter deposition of thin films onto silicon wafeis. or substrates, in the manufacture of integrated circuit chips With the ongoing trend towaid device miniaturization in semiconductor manufacture where device features are currently assuming submicron dimensions and with integrated circuits increasing in functional size, complexity and value, particles ot a size and quantity heretofore tolerable in semiconductor manufacture are now capable of causing damage that can totally destroy expensive devices and, therefore, are no longer tolerable.

Still further, in the process of manufacturing semiconductoi devices on silicon wafers, there are applications in which a need often exists foi sputtering onto the back side of the water For example, gold is sometimes applied on the back of wafeis to facilitate heat removal from the chip Where front side sputtering is taking place, the back side of the wafer is typically sealed against a heating surface built into the wafer holder. During backside sputtenng, however, the front side of the wafer, which contains the devices being manufactured, must not touch the backplane. Wafer holder latches act in concert with the physical elements that define the mounting plane of the wafer holder on which the wafer tests to clamp the wafer between the latches and those elements on the wafer holder. Such latches may include, for example, flexible tabs or a suitable wafer mounting ring The holders include an appropriate wafer exposure opening to permit etching or sputtering of the wafer. In the prior art wafer holders, the inteiaction of the latches and the mounting plane structure has produced a number of the problems discussed above.

The holder of the wafer clamping device typically consists of a multitude of flexing tabs and a plurality of latches, for example, three latches, mounted to the wafer holder housing The flexible tabs define a wafer mounting plane on which the wafer rests When the wafer is loaded onto the wafer holder, a load arm of a robot typically positions the silicon wafer against the tabs in a precise and repeatable manner so as to minimize chipping and piovide tellable wafer latching The wafer is held in place on the holder with friction generated, foi example, by spring loaded rollers forcing the wafer against two adjacent tabs The force applied by such I oilers deflects the wafer locally a small amount in accordance with the thickness of the wafer. Thinner and more flexible wafers tend to induce less friction against the tabs and have a greater tendency to slide during acceleration. If such sliding happens to position a tab at or near the edge of a wafer, wafei chipping can result, particularly when the wafer is sealed against a backplane.

The latch itself can cause problems The major components of a typical latch assembly are the body of the latch with a front roller and one or more rear rollers mounted opposite the front roller or to its
sides The teim "tiont" tollei leteis heiein to a lollei that tolls against a water to latch the wafer to a holdei, and the terms "leai ' lollei and "back" tollei tefei heiein to rolleis that lemain in contact with the holder to guide the latch ot to position the latch by legistiatton with detents on the holder The latch assembly customarily pivots aiound a πgidly fixed post anchored to the wafei holdei. and the assembly is usually held together by a helical spring The body of the latch typically contains a slot which is engaged by actuatoi pins on a loading aim The actuator pins are operated to rotate the latch through an arc of usually 90° to latch and unlatch the latches, moving the front roller into position against or retracted from the wafer In addition to applying force lor holding the wafer m place by urging the front roller against the wafer, the helical spring maintains the latch assembly in an upright position normal to the holder so that unobstructed engagement of the actuator pins with slots in the latch can occur

When the latches are rotated, they slide against stationary wear shims hich are biased by the force of the latch spring The latched and unlatched positions of a typical latch are defined by three detents 90° apart Three equal depth detents ate typically provided on the surface of the holder into which the rollers of the latch assembly are pushed by the torce ot the spring, and a fourth detent, which is deeper, is provided closest to the edge of the wafei The deeper detent allows the wafer engaging portion of the front roller to lowet onto the wafer and apply positive pressure of the wafer against the tabs when the latches are in their latched positions The body of the latch is typically made out of metal, usually stainless steel The rollers are usually provided with a substantially smaller cross-sectional radius than the spherical radius of the detents in order to minimize traction resistance of the rollers All mutually moving elements are also typically made out of metal such as stainless steel and employ sliding pairs with various degrees of fπctional resistance

In use, latch actuation is preceded by the loading of a water onto the wafer holder such that it rests against the tabs Simultaneously, the actuator pins on the transfer arm engage the slots of each of the latches, with the rollers expected to be in full detent and the latches in their open or unlatched positions While the wafer is held with the suction of a vacuum chuck or by some other clamping mechanism on the transfer arm, the latch actuator pms lotate the latches about their pivots. Both rollers of the latch rise out of and descend into a shallow pan: of detents, thus pulling the latches mto and keeping them in the desired orientations However, when the front roller is latched onto the wafer, this function is performed only by the rear roller Generous clearance between the pins and the slots is typical in order to avoid brushing of pms against the slots during the engagement, which is a frequent cause of wafer chipping Due to such oversized slots, the latch rotation is always less than 100% that of the actuator pins The force of the spring is expected to overcome fπctional tesistance of the sliding elements and to pull the rollers fully into the detents, thus completing 100% totation

Every time the edge of a misaligned slot is struck by an actuator pin of the transfer arm, the impact is transmitted to the front roller, which can cause a piece of wafer to be chipped away by the roller bearing agamst the wafer. This results in significant w aste of devices and downtime for cleaning In high vacuum, the use of a slot wider than the pins is not always effective In many situations, high friction

Furthermore, the faction coefficients of materials increase many times in vacuum, and the wear of most materials at temperatures of above 600°C significantly increases, causing non-metals to abrade and metals to gall, causing highly undesirable particle generation, which causes defective fabrication of semiconductoi devices oi possibly misalignment of latches and resulting wafer clipping

It has also been found that the ctoss-secttonal shape of the water-contacting portion of the front loller has direct impact on wafei chipping and particle generation With rounded edge rollers, the tangent point of wafei contact can mo\ e close to the edge ot the wafei where it is more likely to cause the wafer to chip On the othei hand, a cylindrical 1 oiler can cause the roller to roll onto an edge, which can also generate particles by crumbling the edges of the ater or the roller
